lines.text: Your forecast is only as good as the data behind it.
And half of it lives outside NetSuite.
Pipeline in the CRM, headcount in the HR system, drivers in a spreadsheet.
Every month, someone copies and pastes it all into the plan.
NetSuite Planning brings external data straight into the model.
Load a file, map it once, and let the forecast recalculate.
No retyping. Every load validated.
And a full trail of what came in, and when.
Here is how it works.
Start with a file, for example the pipeline export from your CRM: product, region, month, amount and probability.
In Data Exchange, open the integration for that file.
Pick the file and the period to load.
The first time, map the columns to Planning: products to classes, regions to locations.
After that, the mapping is reused every month.
Run the integration.
Planning imports the file, validates every row, and flags anything it cannot map.
Add the missing mapping, run it again, and the load is clean.
Then a rule turns pipeline into forecast.
Amount times probability, by product and by month.
The revenue forecast updates on its own.
And you can see exactly how much of it came from the pipeline.
Once it works, schedule it.
The latest data is in the plan every morning, before anyone logs in.
Write to Bryant Park Consulting to connect your data to NetSuite Planning.
And get the most out of your implementation.
